allows only one reset prepared against the same account revision
atomically creates exactly one account for simultaneous normalized-email requests
binds a self-reset to the authenticated email as well as the account ID and version
checks the current admin active independently at the write boundary
checks the current admin identity independently at the write boundary
checks the current admin role independently at the write boundary
checks the current admin version independently at the write boundary
does not bootstrap after ordinary provisioning commits during its preflight window
does not resurrect old sessions when an account is disabled and re-enabled
executes operator creation, access changes, reset, inspection and repeat-safe migration end to end
identifies malformed initialization metadata instead of failing during implicit string conversion
invalidates prior claims on reset and prevents an older password change from undoing it
keeps independent stores bound to their own table pair without process-global targets
migrates legacy UUID accounts repeatably without activating disabled or unlisted accounts
reads a complete whitelist across real service pages while preserving disabled state and excluding extra fields
refuses ambiguous legacy duplicates before migration changes any mapping
rejects an admin write revoked while the request is in flight
rejects an expiry changed after authorization before committing a password change
reports malformed user fields without serializing the stored hash or password value
reports partial migration progress and safely resumes after interruption
retains the operator credential privately even if a committed transaction loses its response
rolls back the user write if the email claim changes after preflight
supports an administrator resetting their own account without duplicate transaction targets
uses one configured expiry and refuses expired issuance or password changes
writes the exact configured expiry to operator files before committing it
